notes.1-8: The extracts were short, straightforward interactions. Overall, candidates performed well in this exercise. Most candidates answered Questions 1 and 3 well. For Question 2 , three quarters of the candidates were familiar with faire chaud ; option B was the most common error. For Question 4 , many candidates understood soirée disco . Question 5 was also attempted well. There was no pattern in the incorrect answers for those questions. For Question 6 , nearly three quarters of the cohort understood jus de pomme ; C was the most common error. An equal number of candidates recognised boulangerie and answered Question 7 correctly; option A was the most frequent incorrect answer. For Question 8 , many candidates understood tasses and correctly chose A .
notes.9-14: Here candidates heard a longer extract which featured information about a hotel in Brussels. Overall, candidates performed very well in this exercise. For Question 9 , many candidates were familiar with station de métro. Most of those who answered incorrectly chose C . Most candidates answered Questions 10 and 11 successfully. For Question 12 , many candidates understood biscuits . There was no pattern in the incorrect answers. Question 13 was attempted well; those who answered incorrectly often chose A . For Question 14 , many candidates correctly chose C ; option D was the most frequent incorrect answer.
notes.15-19: This was a matching exercise in which candidates heard a conversation between two friends about theme parks. Overall, candidates performed well in this exercise. Question 15 was attempted well and many candidates successfully matched me font toujours rire with statement F . For Question 16 , over three quarters of the cohort understood pour les grands comme pour les petits and successfully chose statement A . For Question 17 , over half the candidates understood déçu and the reference to the past and correctly selected D . For Question 18 , nearly a third of candidates successfully chose statement C ; the most frequent incorrect answer was B , followed by D . For Question 19 , nearly two thirds of the cohort successfully chose statement E . The most common errors were B and D .
notes.20-28: In this exercise, candidates heard an interview with Moncef, who talked about his life and school in Tunis. The exercise represented a step up in the incline of difficulty of the test. Many candidates answered Question 20 successfully and chose C ; most of those who answered incorrectly heard centre-ville and chose distractor B . For Question 21 , nearly half the cohort understood où on répare tout and successfully selected A ; most heard appareils électriques and incorrectly chose distractor B . For Question 22 , almost half the cohort successfully matched se dépêcher with se presser and selected the correct answer B . Distractor A was the most frequent error. Question 23 was attempted well and many candidates correctly selected C ; distractor A was the most frequent incorrect answer. For Question 24 , just under half the cohort understood comme moi and successfully linked the answer to A . Most of those who answered incorrectly chose distractor B : candidates needed to listen carefully as sandwich referred to what some students have for lunch, not Moncef. For Question 25 , more than half the candidates correctly matched je suis un élève sérieux with A ; most of the candidates who answered incorrectly chose distractor B , which described a friend of Moncef’s. Half the cohort successfully answered Question 26 ; distractor B was the most frequent error. Candidates needed to listen carefully as Moncef explained that he was allowed to surf the net once he had finished his schoolwork, which came first at 16h00. For Question 27 , over half the candidates successfully chose A . Most of those who answered incorrectly heard dîner and chose distractor B . Over half the cohort also answered Question 28 correctly and selected C , whilst most of those who answered incorrectly selected distractor B . Candidates needed to listen to the whole sentence as je ne suis pas sûr ruled out B .
notes.29-34: In this extract, candidates heard an interview with Félicia about Parkour, an extreme sport. This was an appropriately demanding exercise at this stage of the paper. Many candidates answered Question 29 correctly and chose B . Nearly two thirds of the candidates answered Question 30 successfully; most of those who answered incorrectly heard 2020 and chose distractor A . Candidates needed to listen carefully as this was when Félicia’s friends started practising the sport. For Question 31 , candidates needed to focus on what Félicia enjoys the most and over two thirds successfully chose C ; distractors B and D were the most frequent errors. Many candidates answered Question 32 well. For Question 33 , nearly three quarters of the candidates successfully chose C . Those who answered incorrectly chose distractors A and B in equal numbers. Question 34 was challenging. Under half the candidates successfully selected A , with distractor C the most frequent incorrect answer.
notes.35-37: In this exercise, candidates heard an interview with Nathan, a young man from Québec who works in Mexico. For each question in this exercise, candidates had to identify two correct statements from a choice of five. This was an appropriately demanding and challenging exercise at this stage of the paper. For Question 35 , nearly half the candidates successfully chose A and over three quarters successfully selected D . Nearly a quarter incorrectly chose distractor B : candidates needed to listen carefully to the tenses as Nathan explained that his parents had already visited him. As many incorrectly chose distractor C , although confiance referred to Nathan lacking self-confidence. For Question 36 , over a third of the candidates correctly chose B and over half successfully selected E . Over half the cohort missed presque and incorrectly chose distractor A . For Question 37 , nearly two thirds of the cohort successfully chose B and over a third successfully chose C . Nearly a third of the candidates incorrectly chose distractor E : they needed to listen carefully as connaître d’autres pays referred to Nathan’s father. A quarter of the candidates incorrectly chose distractor D : candidates needed to listen to the whole sentence as travelling was negated by il n’a pas eu l’occasion.
